answers.explanation: It "pulls the system up by its bootstraps", starting from nothing in memory.
RAM is volatile. Something nonvolatile has to hold the very first instructions the CPU runs.
Firmware sits between hardware and software: code that comes with the machine.
Once the kernel starts, the kernel takes over all scheduling. The bootstrap's work is done.
Both a cold start and a reboot begin by running the bootstrap program.
The bootstrap runs first, initializes everything, then loads the kernel and starts it.
